rules.title: Relocation assistance and Declaration of Intent to Evict for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: Before a no-fault eviction from an RSO or JCO unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD, serve notice only after filing, file a copy of the notice within 3 days, and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of serving notice. For July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 the amounts are $11,000 (eligible, under 3 years), $14,400 (eligible, 3+ years or low income), $23,150 (qualified, under 3 years) and $27,400 (qualified, 3+ years or low income), paid per unit.
rules.key_value: Eligible $11,000 / $14,400; Qualified $23,150 / $27,400 per unit; paid within 15 days of notice
rules.quoted_span:
Failure to file the Landlord Declaration with the LAHD makes the eviction a 
violation of the RSO or JCO.
rules.coverage_text: Units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO); demolition or conversion relocation applies regardless of RSO/JCO coverage under LAMC 47.06 & 47.07.
rules.exemptions: No relocation owed when replacing a resident manager with another resident manager (unless manager-tenant receiving only free/reduced rent), or when eviction is required due to natural-disaster hazardous conditions not caused by landlord negligence. Landlord may offset accumulated unpaid rent except for government orders to vacate or unpermitted-dwelling orders.
rules.penalty: Eviction without the filed Declaration violates the RSO or JCO; tenant may raise failure to pay relocation as an affirmative defense, file an LAHD complaint, or pursue a private right of action.
rules.interaction: Amounts increase every July 1. For demolition of Protected Units for new construction occupied by lower-income tenants, RPO/HCA amounts apply instead if higher.

rules.title: Reduced relocation assistance for Mom and Pop properties (owner/family occupancy evictions)
rules.requirement: For owner or eligible-relative occupancy evictions, Mom and Pop landlords may pay reduced relocation ($10,550 eligible; $21,250 qualified) if the building has four or fewer units, the provision was not used in the previous three years, the landlord owns no more than four units and one single-family home in the City, and the relative owns no residential property in the City.
rules.quoted_span:
The reduced fee for Mom and Pop properties applies only for evictions for occupancy by the 
owner or an eligible relative and only if all of the following conditions exist:
rules.coverage_text: Buildings with four or fewer rental units owned by landlords owning no more than four units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Applies only to evictions for occupancy by owner, family, or manager.

rules.title: One month's rent relocation for JCO single-family dwellings owned by natural persons
rules.requirement: For a JCO-covered single-family dwelling owned by a natural person who owns no more than four dwelling units and one single-family home in the City, relocation assistance is one month's rent in effect when notice was served, paid as money or a credit.
rules.quoted_span:
When the residential real property is a
single-family dwelling subject to the JCO and the owner is a natural person, including natural
persons who hold properties in a trust or registered legal entity controlled by that natural person,
who owns no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in the City
of Los Angeles: one month’s rent that was in effect when the landlord served the written notice
to terminate the tenancy, as either a monetary payment or credit.
rules.coverage_text: Single-family dwellings subject to the JCO owned by natural persons (including via trust or controlled entity) owning no more than four dwelling units and a single-family home on a separate lot in Los Angeles.

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units for new construction
rules.requirement: Owners demolishing a Protected Unit for new construction within 5 years of filing must comply with RPO relocation via one of three options; lower-income households receive standardized payments ($115,480 extremely low, $96,750 very low, $87,450 low income under Option 1), and all tenants receive at least RSO/JCO amounts within 15 days. Owners must pay the higher of State HCA or City amounts.
rules.key_value: $115,480 ELI / $96,750 VLI / $87,450 LI (Option 1); penalties from $250,000 per displaced unit
rules.citation: Ordinances No. 188481 and No. 188482 (Resident Protections Ordinance); Gov. Code 66300 et seq.; LAMC 165.03.I(1)
rules.quoted_span:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO. Failure to comply with the RPO may result in 
financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.coverage_text: Protected Units (including all RSO units, units under affordability covenants or rent control or rented by lower-income households in past five years, or Ellis-withdrawn units in past 10 years) demolished for new construction.
rules.exemptions: Regular RSO/JCO relocation rules apply if units are not Protected Units or not occupied by a lower-income tenant.
rules.penalty: Financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction: Owner must pay the higher of the State Housing Crisis Act (Gov. Code 66300 et seq.) or City amounts; RSO/JCO amounts must be enhanced for lower-income tenants under the HCA regardless of RPO applicability.
rules.conflict_note: Bulletin B's fee chart labels the relocation service fees as effective July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026, while Bulletin A lists identical fees as effective July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027; relocation payment charts in both bulletins state July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
